assessments.reasoning: The retained original handbook was reopened. Its title and issue notice establish the NBS publication and January 1976 date. The foreword classifies MUMPS as a programming language and attributes the narrative specification in Part I to the committee's March 1975 adoption of MDC/28. The opening of Part I confirms its language subject.

challenge.method: Could the expanded acronym identify only a hospital software system, or could January 1976 be the committee adoption date?
challenge.results: The foreword expressly classifies the language and distinguishes committee adoption from handbook issuance. Later names, editions and maintenance status fall outside this identity evidence.

limitations: The identity decision concerns MUMPS as the language. Later standards and the name M require separate sources.
